title: Sabha: Indraprastha
hook: a burning forest, a builder spared, and the promise of a hall

segments.voice: Yesterday, Draupadi's swayamvara ended in a wedding, after Drupada's objection and Vyasa's story. Your line was several reasons, and one silence.

A forest is on fire, and a man runs out of it. He's Maya, an asura and a master builder, with the flames at his back. Krishna, guarding the burning, raises his discus. Maya cries out to Arjuna to save him, and Arjuna answers: don't be afraid. A new book of the Mahabharata opens here, the Sabha Parva, the book of the hall, and it begins with a life spared, and a debt.
screen: `A FOREST ON FIRE.` → `MAYA CRIES OUT.` → `DON'T BE AFRAID.`

segments.voice: First, how the family got here. After the wedding, the Pandavas go back to Hastinapura, alive. Dhritarashtra gives them half the kingdom. Their half is Khandavaprastha, wild land, and there they build a city and call it Indraprastha. Then comes the burning of the Khandava forest, and Maya running out of it. Now, safe, Maya stands before Arjuna: you've saved me. Tell me what I can do for you. Arjuna won't take anything, the text says. In paraphrase: you've done enough; go, and be a friend to me. But Maya presses. He wants to give something. So Arjuna turns it over to Krishna, and Krishna asks for something that isn't for himself. Build a hall, he tells Maya, for Yudhishthira, so fine that no one who studies it could copy it. Here's the word for this new stretch: sabha. It means a hall, and also the assembly that meets in one. Notice how this hall begins. Not with a conquest, but with a life spared in a fire, and a debt the one who's owed doesn't want repaid. Arjuna refuses a reward. Krishna passes it on to the brother who'll sit in that hall as king. A gift handed along twice before a single stone is laid. Today, it's still a promise.
screen: `A CITY BUILT ON WILD LAND.` · `ARJUNA WON'T TAKE A REWARD.` · `KRISHNA ASKS FOR A HALL.` · then, large: `A GIFT HANDED ALONG TWICE.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind a time someone helped you and wouldn't let you pay them back, and wonder where that debt went. Breathe in and remember their kindness; breathe out and picture passing it on, the way Arjuna handed Maya's thanks to Krishna, and Krishna handed it to Yudhishthira. If you pray, you can name them.
Sabha. A hall, and the assembly that gathers in it. Today, the hall at Indraprastha is promised, by a builder spared from a fire.
Your line: a gift handed along twice. The hall starts with a kindness. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Hindu tradition places the Pandavas' city of Indraprastha near present-day Delhi, and the name is still used for places there today.

chat.says: Why did Maya build the Pandavas a hall? Were they paying him?
options: Arjuna wanted no reward for sparing him, so Krishna asked for Yudhishthira's hall.
Dhritarashtra hired him to build it, as part of the half kingdom he gave.
Maya had lost a bet with Arjuna and owed him a building as the price.
chat.meaning: Maya, spared from the Khandava fire, wanted to repay Arjuna. Arjuna refused, and Krishna passed the gift on as a hall for Yudhishthira.

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli: Maya flees the Khandava fire, Krishna raises his discus, Maya appeals to Arjuna, who tells him not to fear.
Confirm Arjuna's refusal ('be a friend to me') and Krishna's request for a hall no one could imitate, built for Yudhishthira.
